salpeterkrieg#summary: Chile defeats Peru and Bolivia in the struggle for the nitrate-rich Atacama Desert; Bolivia loses its access to the sea.
salpeterkrieg#text: The Atacama Desert held rich deposits of nitrate, which was in demand worldwide as fertiliser and for explosives. When Bolivia raised taxes on a Chilean nitrate company, Chile occupied the port of Antofagasta in 1879; Peru supported Bolivia as its ally. Chile won control of the sea and occupied Lima in 1881. In the Treaty of Ancón of 1883 Peru had to cede the province of Tarapacá, and in the truce of 1884 Bolivia lost its coastal province. The loss of access to the sea still burdens relations between Bolivia and Chile today.
schlacht-von-isandlwana#summary: The army of the Zulu king Cetshwayo defeats a British invasion force but cannot win the war.
schlacht-von-isandlwana#text: To end the independence of the Zulu kingdom, Britain presented King Cetshwayo with an impossible ultimatum at the end of 1878 and invaded in January 1879. On 22 January some 20,000 Zulu warriors surprised a British camp at the hill of Isandlwana and destroyed the force; more than 1,300 soldiers and auxiliaries were killed. It was one of the heaviest defeats ever suffered by a European army against an African force. Britain sent reinforcements and defeated the Zulu at Ulundi in July 1879. Cetshwayo was captured and the Zulu kingdom was divided into small chiefdoms.
masseneinwanderung-nach-argentinien#summ: Millions of Europeans, above all from Italy and Spain, emigrate to the Río de la Plata and fundamentally change Argentina.
masseneinwanderung-nach-argentinien#text: Argentina deliberately recruited European settlers to farm the wide plains of the Pampas, which had been opened up after campaigns against Indigenous peoples. Between 1880 and the First World War several million immigrants arrived, many of them only for one harvest season. Wheat and beef became the most important exports, transported on a rapidly growing railway network. Buenos Aires developed into one of the largest cities in the Americas, and the tango emerged in its port districts. Uruguay and southern Brazil experienced similar waves of immigration.
bismarcks-sozialgesetze#summary: The German Empire becomes the first state in the world to introduce health, accident and pension insurance.
bismarcks-sozialgesetze#text: Bismarck pursued a twofold strategy: with the Anti-Socialist Law of 1878 he banned the Social Democrats, while with the social legislation he sought to show workers that the state was looking after them. Health insurance came in 1883, accident insurance in 1884 and old-age and invalidity insurance in 1889, which paid a small pension from the age of 70. Employers and employees paid contributions, and the state added subsidies. The Social Democrats were not won over and became the strongest party in 1890, but the model of social insurance found imitators throughout the world and remains the foundation of the German welfare state to this day.
berliner-konferenz-afrika#summary: The European powers agree in Berlin on rules for dividing Africa into colonies.
berliner-konferenz-afrika#text: At Bismarck's invitation, representatives of 13 European states and the United States met in order to avoid conflict over the Congo and the African coasts. Not a single African took part. The conference laid down that territorial claims had to be backed by actual occupation, and thereby set off the scramble for Africa. By around 1914 every territory on the continent apart from Ethiopia and Liberia was under European rule.
kongo-freistaat#title: Congo Free State under Leopold II
kongo-freistaat#summary: The Belgian king receives the Congo as personal property and exploits it through a brutal system of forced labor.
kongo-freistaat#text: At the Berlin Conference in 1885 the powers recognized the Congo Free State as the personal property of Leopold II, who promised to promote trade and civilization. In reality his colonial troops forced the population to deliver rubber and ivory; those who failed to meet the quotas were flogged, mutilated or killed, and entire villages were burned down. Through violence, forced labor, hunger and disease, several million people are estimated to have died. Reports by the British consul Roger Casement and the campaign of Edmund Morel caused an international scandal, so that Belgium took over the colony in 1908.
benz-patent-motorwagen#title: Carl Benz Builds the First Automobile
benz-patent-motorwagen#summary: In Mannheim, Carl Benz files a patent for a three-wheeled vehicle with a gasoline engine.
benz-patent-motorwagen#text: On 29 January 1886 Carl Benz received the patent for his vehicle powered by a gas engine, the first practical car with an internal combustion engine; at almost the same time Gottlieb Daimler and Wilhelm Maybach built a motor carriage in Cannstatt. In August 1888 Bertha Benz drove with her sons from Mannheim to Pforzheim without her husband's knowledge, the first long-distance journey by automobile, and proved that it was suitable for everyday use. The car stood for the second Industrial Revolution, in which electricity, chemistry and the internal combustion engine reinvented the technology of daily life. With Ford's assembly line it became a mass product from 1913 onward.
lei-aurea-abschaffung-der-sklaverei#summ: With the “Golden Law”, slavery ends in Brazil, the last country in the Americas to abolish it.
lei-aurea-abschaffung-der-sklaverei#text: Brazil had received more enslaved Africans than any other country in the Americas. After the end of the slave trade in 1850 and the law of 1871 that declared the children of enslaved mothers free, pressure from the abolitionists grew, and many enslaved people fled the plantations. On 13 May 1888 Princess Isabel, acting as regent, signed the Lei Áurea, which abolished slavery without compensating the owners. The freed people, however, received neither land nor education. Resentful planters supported the overthrow of the monarchy and the proclamation of the republic the following year.
frauenwahlrecht-neuseeland#summary: New Zealand becomes the first country in the world to grant all women the right to vote in national elections.
frauenwahlrecht-neuseeland#text: In 1893 the women's rights campaigner Kate Sheppard and her fellow activists collected almost 32,000 signatures for a petition, at the time a quarter of all adult women in New Zealand. On 19 September 1893 the governor signed the electoral law, and as early as November women, among them Maori women, voted for parliament for the first time. South Australia followed in 1894, and Finland in 1906 as the first European country; in Germany and Britain it took until 1918. The success in New Zealand became a model for the women's movement around the world.
kubanischer-unabhaengigkeitskrieg#summar: José Martí and his comrades begin the last war against Spanish colonial rule in the Americas.
kubanischer-unabhaengigkeitskrieg#text: From New York José Martí had founded the Cuban Revolutionary Party and won over exiles, workers and veterans for a new uprising. The war began in February 1895; Martí landed in Cuba in April and fell as early as May at Dos Ríos. Spain had large parts of the rural population relocated into camps, where many people died of hunger and disease. In 1898 the United States intervened and defeated Spain within a few months. Cuba became formally independent in 1902 but remained under strong influence from the United States.
hedschasbahn#summary: A railway from Damascus to Medina is meant to make the journey easier for pilgrims and to bind the Arab provinces more closely to Istanbul.
hedschasbahn#text: In 1900 Abdülhamid II had construction begin on a railway line from Damascus into the Hejaz. It was financed to a large extent by donations from Muslims all over the world, whom the sultan, as caliph, called on for support. In September 1908 the line, about 1,300 kilometres long, reached Medina; the planned extension to Mecca was never built. The railway shortened the pilgrimage from weeks to days and made troop transports easier. In the First World War Arab insurgents attacked it again and again.
boxeraufstand#summary: An uprising against foreigners and Christians in China is put down jointly by eight powers.
boxeraufstand#text: The secret society known as the Boxers turned against missionaries, railways and the growing control of the great powers over China. In June 1900, after the German envoy had been murdered, Boxers and imperial troops besieged the legation quarter in Beijing for 55 days. An expeditionary force from eight states, among them Japan, Russia, Britain, the United States and Germany, captured Beijing and plundered the city; Emperor William II had urged the German troops to show no mercy in his Hun speech. The Boxer Protocol of 1901 forced China to pay enormous reparations and accelerated the decline of the Qing dynasty, which was overthrown in 1911.
erster-motorflug-wright#title: First Powered Flight by the Wright Brothers
erster-motorflug-wright#summary: Orville and Wilbur Wright achieve the first controlled powered flight at Kitty Hawk.
erster-motorflug-wright#text: On 17 December 1903 Orville Wright lifted off from the beach at Kitty Hawk in North Carolina for twelve seconds in the Flyer he had built himself. The two bicycle mechanics had experimented with gliders for years and had developed a system for controlling the aircraft about all three axes. Aircraft were already used militarily in the First World War, and within a few decades aviation fundamentally changed both travel and warfare.
beginn-des-panamakanalbaus#title: Construction of the Panama Canal begins
beginn-des-panamakanalbaus#summary: After Panama breaks away from Colombia, the United States begins building a canal between the Atlantic and the Pacific.
beginn-des-panamakanalbaus#text: A French company under Ferdinand de Lesseps had failed in the 1880s because of the terrain, yellow fever and malaria, and financial problems. When Colombia rejected a treaty with the United States, Washington supported the independence of Panama in 1903 and received control of a canal zone in return. In 1904 the United States took over the construction site. Measures against mosquitoes pushed back the epidemics, and tens of thousands of workers, mainly from the Caribbean, dug the canal. In 1914 the first ship passed through the new waterway.
voelkermord-herero-nama#title: Genocide of the Herero and Nama
voelkermord-herero-nama#summary: German colonial troops destroy a large part of the Herero and Nama in German South West Africa.
voelkermord-herero-nama#text: After the seizure of their land and the loss of their rights, the Herero rose up in January 1904 against German colonial rule in what is now Namibia. After the Battle of Waterberg, General Lothar von Trotha drove them into the waterless Omaheke Desert and ordered that every Herero be shot. Survivors, and later the Nama who had also risen up, were forced into labor in concentration camps. Up to 80 percent of the Herero and half of the Nama lost their lives; in 2021 the Federal Republic of Germany recognized the crimes as genocide.
jungtuerkische-revolution#summary: Officers of the Committee of Union and Progress force Sultan Abdülhamid II to put the constitution of 1876 back into force.
jungtuerkische-revolution#text: In the summer of 1908 officers in Macedonia who belonged to the secret Committee of Union and Progress mutinied and threatened to march on Istanbul. On 24 July 1908 Abdülhamid II put the constitution back into force, and throughout the empire Muslims, Christians and Jews celebrated the new freedom together. Soon afterwards the empire lost Bosnia to Austria-Hungary, and Bulgaria declared its independence. After a failed counter-coup Abdülhamid was deposed in 1909. From 1913 the Young Turks Enver, Talat and Cemal dominated the state.
beginn-der-mexikanischen-revolution#summ: Francisco Madero calls for an uprising against the long-time ruler Porfirio Díaz and sets off a revolution lasting years.
beginn-der-mexikanischen-revolution#text: Porfirio Díaz had ruled Mexico almost without interruption since 1876; under him railways, mining and foreign investment grew, but most peasants lost their land to large haciendas. When Díaz had himself re-elected yet again in 1910, Francisco Madero, the son of a landowning family, called for an armed uprising on 20 November. Peasant armies under Emiliano Zapata in the south and Pancho Villa in the north joined in, and Díaz resigned in 1911. A decade of civil wars followed in which hundreds of thousands died. The Constitution of 1917 brought land reform and workers' rights.
balkankriege#summary: An alliance of the Balkan states conquers almost all the remaining European territories of the Ottoman Empire.
balkankriege#text: While the empire was still fighting Italy over Libya, Bulgaria, Serbia, Greece and Montenegro attacked in October 1912. Within a few weeks the Ottomans lost Macedonia, Albania and Thrace up to the outskirts of Istanbul; Albania declared its independence in November 1912. In the Second Balkan War of 1913 the victors quarrelled over the spoils, and the Ottomans regained Edirne. Hundreds of thousands of Muslim refugees came to Anatolia. The defeats radicalized the Young Turk leadership.
fliessband-ford#title: First Automobile Assembly Line at Ford
fliessband-ford#summary: Henry Ford introduces the moving assembly line in Detroit for production of the Model T.
fliessband-ford#text: At the Highland Park plant, Henry Ford had the chassis of the Model T pulled past the workers on a rope, each of them performing just one operation. The time needed to assemble a car fell from more than twelve hours to about one and a half. The car became so cheap that workers too could afford one. Assembly-line production became the model for mass production in the 20th century.
attentat-von-sarajevo#summary: The murder of the Austrian heir to the throne, Franz Ferdinand, triggers the First World War.
attentat-von-sarajevo#text: On 28 June 1914 the Serbian nationalist Gavrilo Princip shot dead the heir to the throne, Franz Ferdinand, and his wife Sophie in Sarajevo. Backed by Germany, Austria-Hungary issued an ultimatum to Serbia and declared war on 28 July. Through the alliances between Russia and Serbia, France and Russia, and Britain and Belgium, the conflict widened into a European war within a week. The July Crisis is regarded as an example of how the automatic workings of alliances and misjudgments can lead to a great war that nobody wanted.
marneschlacht-und-stellungskrieg#title: Battle of the Marne and the Beginning of Trench Warfare
marneschlacht-und-stellungskrieg#summary: The German advance on Paris is halted at the Marne; the Western Front freezes into trench warfare for four years.
marneschlacht-und-stellungskrieg#text: According to the Schlieffen Plan, the German army was to defeat France in six weeks by advancing through Belgium, before Russia was fully mobilized in the east. At the beginning of September 1914 German troops stood 40 kilometers from Paris, but from 5 to 12 September French and British forces threw them back in the Battle of the Marne, with Parisian taxis bringing reinforcements to the front. In the east Hindenburg and Ludendorff had won at Tannenberg, but the chance of a quick victory in the west had been lost. After a race to the sea, both sides dug into trenches by the end of the year along 700 kilometers from the North Sea to the Swiss border, and machine guns, barbed wire and artillery turned every attack into mass death.
schlacht-um-gallipoli#summary: The Allied landing at the Dardanelles fails against the Ottoman defense and costs more than 100,000 lives.
schlacht-um-gallipoli#text: In order to force the Ottoman Empire out of the war and open a sea route to Russia, British and French ships attempted in the spring of 1915 to force the straits of the Dardanelles. When this failed, British, French, Australian and New Zealand troops landed on the Gallipoli peninsula on 25 April 1915. The Ottoman defenders, among them Colonel Mustafa Kemal, held the heights, and the fighting froze as it had on the Western Front. In January 1916 the Allies evacuated the peninsula; more than 100,000 soldiers on both sides were dead. In Australia and New Zealand 25 April is still commemorated today as Anzac Day, and for Turkey the victory became a founding myth.
voelkermord-an-den-armeniern#summary: The Young Turk government has the Armenian population of the Ottoman Empire deported and murdered.
voelkermord-an-den-armeniern#text: On 24 April 1915 the government of the Committee of Union and Progress had hundreds of Armenian intellectuals and politicians arrested in Constantinople, and most of them were later killed. The Armenian communities of Anatolia were then sent on death marches into the Syrian desert on the pretext of wartime security; men were shot, while women, children and the elderly died of hunger, thirst and violence or in camps near Deir ez-Zor. Estimates put the number of dead at around one million, and there were also mass killings of Assyrians and Greeks. The allied German Empire was informed through its diplomats and officers but did not intervene. The historian Raphael Lemkin later coined the term genocide with this crime and the Holocaust in mind; the German Bundestag recognized the genocide in 2016, while Turkey disputes the term to this day.
schlacht-um-verdun#summary: Ten months of industrialized battle over the French fortress claim more than 700,000 dead and wounded.
schlacht-um-verdun#text: In February 1916 the German high command attacked the fortress of Verdun in order to bleed the French army dry in a battle of attrition. Both sides fired millions of shells onto a few square kilometers of ground; villages disappeared completely. When the fighting ended in December, the front ran almost unchanged. Verdun became a symbol of the futility of trench warfare and later of Franco-German reconciliation.
balfour-erklaerung#summary: Britain promises the Jews a national home in Palestine and thereby lays the ground for the Middle East conflict.
balfour-erklaerung#text: On 2 November 1917 the British foreign secretary Arthur Balfour stated in a letter to Lord Rothschild that the government viewed with favor the establishment of a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine, without prejudice to the rights of the non-Jewish communities living there. The pledge was intended to win the Zionist movement and the Jewish public in the United States and Russia over to the war effort. At the same time Britain had held out the prospect of a state of their own to the Arabs in return for their revolt against the Ottomans, and in the Sykes-Picot Agreement had secretly divided the Middle East into spheres of influence with France. In 1920 Britain received the League of Nations mandate over Palestine; growing Jewish immigration and the resistance of the Arab population led to the first violent clashes in the 1920s and 1930s.
kriegseintritt-usa-1917#title: Entry of the United States into the War
kriegseintritt-usa-1917#summary: After the unrestricted submarine warfare, the United States declares war on Germany.
kriegseintritt-usa-1917#text: President Woodrow Wilson had kept the United States out of the war for years. When Germany resumed unrestricted submarine warfare in February 1917 and the Zimmermann Telegram revealed a German offer of alliance to Mexico, Congress declared war on 6 April 1917. More than two million American soldiers and the industrial strength of the United States tipped the balance of power in favor of the Entente.
russische-revolution#summary: The tsar is overthrown, and in October the Bolsheviks under Lenin seize power.
russische-revolution#text: Hunger, war weariness and strikes forced Tsar Nicholas II to abdicate in March 1917; a provisional government, however, continued the war. Lenin, whom the German government allowed to travel from exile in Switzerland to Russia, demanded peace, land and all power to the soviets. In November the Bolsheviks overthrew the government in Petrograd. There followed the peace of Brest-Litovsk, a bloody civil war and, in 1922, the founding of the Soviet Union.
novemberrevolution-1918#summary: Mutinying sailors and striking workers overthrow the monarchy; Germany becomes a republic and introduces women's suffrage.
novemberrevolution-1918#text: When the naval command wanted to send the fleet out at the end of October 1918 for a final battle against England, the sailors in Wilhelmshaven and Kiel refused the order. Within a few days the revolt spread across the whole empire: workers' and soldiers' councils took power in the cities, the princes abdicated, and on 9 November Philipp Scheidemann proclaimed the republic in Berlin, while a few hours later Karl Liebknecht proclaimed a socialist republic. Friedrich Ebert took over the government as the Council of People's Deputies, which on 12 November announced the eight-hour day and the right to vote for women. The labor movement broke apart over the question of whether Germany should become a parliamentary democracy or a council republic; in January 1919 the government had the Spartacist uprising crushed by Freikorps units, and Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht were murdered.
spanische-grippe#summary: A worldwide influenza pandemic claims more lives than the First World War.
spanische-grippe#text: In the spring of 1918 a new influenza appeared in military camps in the United States and on the Western Front, spreading across the whole world with troop transports. It got its name because the newspapers of neutral Spain, free of wartime censorship, reported on the disease in detail. In a second, far deadlier wave in the autumn of 1918, unusually many young adults died of pneumonia within a few days. By 1920 about a third of the world's population had been infected, and at least 20 to 50 million people died, particularly many of them in India. Schools, theaters and churches were closed and masks were made compulsory, but without antibiotics and vaccines medicine remained largely powerless.
waffenstillstand-compiegne#summary: On 11 November 1918 the guns fall silent on the Western Front; the First World War is over.
waffenstillstand-compiegne#text: After the failure of the German spring offensive and the collapse of its allies, the Supreme Army Command itself called for an armistice in the autumn of 1918. In Germany sailors mutinied, workers' and soldiers' councils took power, and on 9 November the republic was proclaimed; William II fled to the Netherlands. In a railway carriage in the forest of Compiègne the German delegation signed the harsh conditions set by the Allies. They came into force at 11 o'clock on 11 November.
gruendung-des-bauhauses#summary: Walter Gropius founds a school in Weimar that links art, craft and industry and establishes modern design.
gruendung-des-bauhauses#text: In April 1919 the architect Walter Gropius merged the academy of art and the school of arts and crafts in Weimar into the Staatliches Bauhaus, whose manifesto set out the aim of bringing all the arts together under the roof of building. Teachers such as Wassily Kandinsky, Paul Klee, Lyonel Feininger and László Moholy-Nagy, and workshop masters such as the weaver Gunta Stölzl and the metal designer Marianne Brandt, designed furniture, lamps, tableware and typefaces for industrial mass production. In 1925 the school moved into the building in Dessau designed by Gropius, and in 1932 to Berlin, where the National Socialists closed it in 1933. Many members of the Bauhaus emigrated and carried the school's ideas to the United States, to Israel and around the world; the Bauhaus became a symbol of the Golden Twenties and of modernism.
weimarer-verfassung#title: National Assembly and the Weimar Constitution
weimarer-verfassung#summary: The first German democracy receives its constitution; for the first time women vote and enter parliament.
weimarer-verfassung#text: On 19 January 1919 Germans elected a constituent national assembly, in which women took part as voters and candidates for the first time; 37 of them were elected. Because there was unrest in Berlin, the parliament met in the National Theatre in Weimar, elected Friedrich Ebert as Reich President and on 19 February heard Marie Juchacz give the first speech by a woman in a German parliament. The constitution signed on 11 August 1919 made Germany a parliamentary republic with universal suffrage from the age of 20, fundamental rights, referendums and a strong, directly elected Reich President. Article 48 on emergency decrees and the system of pure proportional representation, which brought many small parties into parliament, later proved to be weak points that the opponents of the republic exploited.
versailler-vertrag#summary: The peace treaty imposes territorial losses, disarmament, reparations and war guilt on Germany.
versailler-vertrag#text: The victorious powers negotiated the treaty without German participation and forced the government of the young Weimar Republic to sign it on 28 June 1919. Germany lost Alsace-Lorraine, large parts of West Prussia and Posen as well as all its colonies, was allowed to maintain an army of only 100,000 men and had to pay reparations. Article 231 assigned responsibility for the war to Germany and its allies. Nationalists used the treaty as a dictated peace of shame in their propaganda against the republic.
gruendung-voelkerbund#title: Founding of the League of Nations
gruendung-voelkerbund#summary: The first worldwide organization for securing peace begins its work in Geneva.
gruendung-voelkerbund#text: The League of Nations went back to Woodrow Wilson's Fourteen Points and was intended to resolve conflicts through negotiation, arbitration and joint sanctions. The United States of all countries never joined, because the Senate rejected the treaty; Germany was admitted only in 1926 and the Soviet Union in 1934. Without troops of its own, the League was unable to prevent the acts of aggression by Japan, Italy and Germany in the 1930s. Its subsidiary organizations for labor, health and refugees lived on in the United Nations.
abschaffung-des-sultanats#summary: The Grand National Assembly in Ankara declares the sultanate abolished; the last sultan, Mehmed VI, leaves Istanbul.
abschaffung-des-sultanats#text: After the defeat in the First World War the Allies had occupied Istanbul and in the Treaty of Sèvres in 1920 had provided for the partition of Anatolia. The national movement under Mustafa Kemal formed a rival government in Ankara and won the War of Independence. On 1 November 1922 the Grand National Assembly resolved to abolish the sultanate. Mehmed VI fled on 17 November aboard a British warship; his cousin Abdülmecid II remained only caliph until the caliphate too was abolished in 1924. After more than 600 years the rule of the House of Osman thus came to an end.
gruendung-tuerkische-republik#title: Founding of the Republic of Turkey
gruendung-tuerkische-republik#summary: The secular Republic of Turkey emerges under Mustafa Kemal from the collapsed Ottoman Empire.
gruendung-tuerkische-republik#text: The Ottoman Empire had lost the war at Germany's side and was to be largely partitioned under the Treaty of Sèvres. Mustafa Kemal organized the resistance, defeated the Greek troops in Anatolia and secured the present-day borders in the Treaty of Lausanne in 1923. On 29 October 1923 the republic was proclaimed. Kemal abolished the sultanate and the caliphate, separated religion and state, and introduced the Latin alphabet and women's suffrage.
krisenjahr-1923#title: The Crisis Year 1923: Occupation of the Ruhr, Hyperinflation and the Hitler Putsch
krisenjahr-1923#summary: The mark becomes worthless, France occupies the Ruhr region, and in Munich Hitler attempts a coup.
